facts.raw_span: A 33-year-old man with no significant past medical history
presented with a 3-month history of progressively worsening occipital headache
exacerbated by Valsalva maneuvers
bilateral past-pointing and an intention tremor
a 6.9 × 5.5 × 6.1 cm lobulated mass centered at the left cerebellopontine angle
extending craniocaudally from the left ambient cistern to the premedullary space
multiloculated T1-hypointense, T2-FLAIR–partially suppressible nonenhancing cystic areas
T1/T2-isointense enhancing solid components
curvilinear signal loss with corresponding T1 hyperintensity consistent with hemorrhagic foci
compression of the left cerebellum and brainstem
dilation of the third, fourth, and lateral ventricles
smooth remodeling and erosion of the left petrous apex, clivus, carotid canal, and foramen ovale

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings, including a lobulated mass at the left cerebellopontine angle and smooth remodeling and erosion of the left petrous apex, are consistent with an acoustic neuroma.
The patient's imaging findings, including a multiloculated mass with cystic areas and solid components, are consistent with a meningioma.
The patient's imaging findings, including curvilinear signal loss with corresponding T1 hyperintensity consistent with hemorrhagic foci, are consistent with a hemangioma.
The patient's imaging findings, including a mass at the left cerebellopontine angle and smooth remodeling and erosion of the left petrous apex, are consistent with a chordoma.
The patient's symptoms, including bilateral past-pointing and an intention tremor, are consistent with a trigeminal schwannoma.
The patient's imaging findings, including a multiloculated mass with cystic areas, are consistent with an epidermoid cyst.
The patient's imaging findings, including a multiloculated mass with cystic areas, are consistent with an arachnoid cyst.
The patient's imaging findings, including smooth remodeling and erosion of the left petrous apex, are consistent with a petrous apex cholesterol granuloma.

The lesion's extension craniocaudally from the left ambient cistern to the premedullary space and the dilation of the third, fourth, and lateral ventricles are consistent with a chordoma, which is a rare tumor that can occur in the clivus and cause such neurological symptoms.

The presence of T1/T2-isointense enhancing solid components within the lesion, combined with its location and the erosion of the petrous apex, is suggestive of a petrous apex chondrosarcoma, a rare malignant tumor that can occur in this region.

rationales.F04: Bilateral past-pointing and intention tremor suggest cerebellar involvement, which is more typical of Trigeminal Schwannoma and Acoustic Neuroma.
rationales.F05: A large lobulated mass at the cerebellopontine angle is highly suggestive of a tumor, with several options being possible including Acoustic Neuroma, Meningioma, and others.
rationales.F07: Multiloculated cystic areas with enhancing septa are more typical of certain tumors like Epidermoid Cyst and Arachnoid Cyst, but can also be seen in other lesions.
rationales.F12: Smooth remodeling and erosion of the petrous apex, clivus, carotid canal, and foramen ovale, along with calcifications, are highly suggestive of a Chordoma or a Petrous Apex Chondrosarcoma.
